zh: 三个人面面相觑，都猜到了是怎么回事？七姑奶奶遇到这种情形，却很沉着，反安慰她说∶『素香，你不要急！有话慢慢说。』『奶奶不见了！』素香用带哭的声音说，『不晓得到哪里去了？』叫她慢慢说，她说得还是没头没脑，七姑奶奶只好问道∶『你怎么知道你奶奶不见了？她什么时候出的门？』『老爷一走，没有多少时候，她叫我到香粉弄去买丝线；又差阿祥去叫米叫柴。等到我跟阿祥回来，她已经不知道什么时候出门了；连门上都不知道，再看后门；是半开在那里。一直到下半天三点钟都不见回来；我进房去一看，一只小首饰箱不见了，替换衣服也少了好些。这——这——！』素香着急地，不知如何表达她的想法。这不用说，自然是到老师太那里去了。七姑奶奶倒吸一口冷气，怔怔地望着同伴；怡情老二便问∶『素香，你们老爷知道不知道？』『不知道。』素香答说∶『阿祥跟轿班去寻老爷去了。』『你们老爷在钱庄里。』七姑奶奶说，『你看，轿班还有哪个在？赶快去通知；请你们老爷到这里来，我有要紧话说。』
en: The three women exchanged glances. Each guessed what had happened. In such a situation the Seventh Lady remained calm and even comforted the maid. “Suxiang, do not be frightened. Tell us slowly.” “Madam has disappeared!” Suxiang said, almost in tears. “No one knows where she has gone.” Asked to speak slowly, she still began in the middle of the story. The Seventh Lady had to question her. “How do you know she has disappeared? When did she leave?” “Not long after Master went out, she sent me to buy silk thread in Xiangfen Lane and sent A’xiang to order rice and firewood. When we came back, she had already gone. No one knew when she had left, not even the man at the front door. Then we looked at the back door and found it half open. By three this afternoon she still had not returned. I went into her room: a small jewelry box was missing, and quite a few changes of clothes. That—that—” Too anxious to explain, Suxiang faltered. There was no need to say it: she must have gone to the elderly abbess. The Seventh Lady drew in a sharp breath and stared at her companions. The Second Miss asked, “Suxiang, does your master know?” “No. A’xiang and the chairmen have gone to look for him.” “Your master is at the bank,” the Seventh Lady said. “See whether any of the chairmen are still here. Send someone to tell him at once. Ask him to come here; I have something important to say.”

zh: 就在这时候，雪岩已经赶到；同来的还有萧家骥。胡雪岩跟怡情老二熟识，与阿金却是初见，不过此时亦无暇细问，同时因为有生客在，要格外镇静，免得『家丑』外扬，所以只点点头，平静地问∶『你们两位怎么也来了？』『我们是碰上的。』七姑奶奶答说，『有话到里面去说。』进入客厅，她方为胡雪岩引见阿金。话要说到紧要地方了，却不宜让素香与阿祥听到；所以她要求跟胡雪岩单独谈话。『阿巧姐去的地方，我知道，在法华镇，一座尼姑庵里，事不宜迟，现在就要去寻她。我看，『七姑奶奶踌躇着说，』只好我跟阿金姐两个人去；你不宜跟她见面。『胡雪岩大惑不解，』到底怎么回事？『他问∶』何以你又知道她的行踪？那位阿金姐，又是怎么回事？『『这时候没有办法细说。小爷叔，你只安排我们到法华好了。』
en: At that moment Hu arrived, accompanied by Xiao Jiaji. He knew the Second Miss well but had never met A’jin. There was no time for inquiries; indeed, the presence of a stranger made him all the more determined to remain composed and keep his domestic troubles from becoming public. He merely nodded and asked quietly, “How do you two come to be here as well?” “We happened to meet,” the Seventh Lady replied. “Let us talk inside.” In the sitting room she introduced A’jin. They were approaching matters that Suxiang and A’xiang ought not to hear, so she asked to speak with Hu privately. “I know where A’qiao has gone—to a convent in Fahua Town. We must lose no time; someone must go for her at once. I think—” She hesitated. “It had better be just Sister A’jin and me. You ought not to meet her.” Hu was utterly bewildered. “What has happened? How do you know where she is? And who is this Sister A’jin?” “There is no time to explain everything now. Little Uncle, just arrange for us to get to Fahua.”

zh: 『法华一带都是安庆来的淮军。还不知道好走不好走呢！』『不要紧！』萧家骥说，『我去一趟好了。』『好极！你去最好。』七姑奶奶很高兴地说；因为萧家骥跟淮军首领很熟，此去必定有许多方便。『七姐，我想我还是应该去。』胡雪岩说，『不见面不要紧，至少让她知道我不是不关心她。你看呢？』『我是怕你们见了面吵起来，弄得局面很不好收场。既然小爷叔这么说，去了也不要紧。』到得法华镇，已经黄昏。萧家骥去找淮军大将程家启部下的一个营官，姓朱；人很爽朗热心，问明来意，请他们吃了一顿饭，然后命手下一个把总将地保老胡找了来，说知究竟。
en: “The whole Fahua district is occupied by Anhui Army troops from Anqing. I do not even know whether we can get through.” “That does not matter,” Xiao said. “I shall go.” “Excellent! You are the best person.” The Seventh Lady was delighted. Xiao knew the Anhui Army commanders well, and his presence would make many things easier. “Seventh Sister, I still think I ought to go,” Hu said. “I need not see her, but at least let her know that I am not indifferent. What do you think?” “I was afraid you would quarrel if you met and make matters impossible to resolve. Since you put it that way, Little Uncle, there is no harm in your going.” It was dusk when they reached Fahua Town. Xiao sought out a battalion commander named Zhu, who served under the Anhui Army general Cheng Xueqi. A frank and helpful man, Zhu heard their errand, gave them a meal, then ordered a subordinate officer, a bazong, to fetch the local constable, Old Hu, and explain what was needed.

zh: 『好的，好的！我来领路。』老胡说道∶『请三位跟我来。』于是迎着月色，往东面去；走不多远，折进一条巷子，巷底有处人家，一带粉墙，墙内花木繁盛，新月微光，影影绰绰；薰风过处，传来一阵浓郁的『夜来香』的香味，每个人都觉得精神一振，而一颗心却无缘无故地飘荡不定，有着一种说不出的胀满的感觉。这份感觉以萧家骥为尤甚，不由得便问∶『这是什么地方？』『这里？』地保答道∶『就是白衣庵。晚上来，要走边门。』边门是一道厚实的木板门，举手可及的上方，有个不为人所注意的扁圆形铁环；地保一伸手拉了两下，只听『克啷、克啷』的响声。不久，听得脚步声、然后门开一线，有人问道∶『哪位？』『小音，是我！』『噢！』门内小音问道∶『老胡，这辰光来做啥？』『你有没有看见客人？』地保指着后面的人说，『你跟了尘师父去说，是我带来的人。』
en: “Certainly, certainly. I shall show the way,” Old Hu said. “The three of you, please follow me.” They headed east in the moonlight and soon turned into a lane. At its far end stood a residence behind a whitewashed wall, with luxuriant flowers and trees inside. In the faint light of the new moon, the shapes were indistinct. A warm breeze carried out the rich scent of night-blooming flowers. Everyone felt suddenly refreshed, yet for no reason their hearts grew restless, filled with a swelling emotion they could not name. Xiao felt it most strongly. “What is this place?” he could not help asking. “Here? White-Robed Convent. At night we use the side entrance.” The side entrance had a solid wooden door. Above it, within reach, was an inconspicuous flattened iron ring. Old Hu reached up and pulled it twice. Clang, clang. After a little while came footsteps; the door opened a crack, and someone asked, “Who is it?” “Xiaoyin, it is me.” “Oh. Old Hu, what brings you here at this hour?” “Can you not see the visitors?” He pointed behind him. “Tell Sister Liaochen that I have brought them.”

zh: 门『呀』地一声开了。灯光照处，小音是个俗家打扮的垂发女郎；等客人都进了门，将门关上；然后一言不发地往前走，穿过一条花径，越过两条走廊，到了一处禅房，看样子是待客之处；她停了下去，看着地保老胡。老胡略有些踌躇，『总爷！』他哈腰问∶『是不是我陪着你老在这里坐一坐？』这何消说得？那把总自然照办。于是老胡跟小音悄悄说了几句；然后示意胡雪岩跟着小音走。穿过禅房，便是一个大院子∶绕向西边的回廊，但见人影、花影一齐映在雪白的粉墙上；还有一头猫的影子，弓起背，正在东面屋脊上『叫春』。萧家骥用手肘轻轻将胡雪岩撞了一下，同时口中在念∶『「曲径通幽处，禅房花木深」！』胡雪岩也看出这白衣庵大有蹊跷。但萧家骥的行径，近乎佻亻达；不是礼佛之道，便咳嗽一声，示意他检点。于是默默地随着小音进入另一座院落，一庭树木，三楹精舍，檀香花香，交杂飘送；萧家骥不由得失声赞道∶『好雅致的地方！』『请里面坐。』小音揭开门帘肃客，『我去请了尘师父来。』说完，她又管自己走了。
en: The door swung open with a creak. By the light they saw Xiaoyin, a girl in ordinary secular dress with her hair hanging loose. Once the visitors were inside, she shut the door and led them forward without a word, along a flower-lined path and through two covered passages to a monastic room apparently used for receiving guests. There she stopped and looked at Old Hu. He hesitated a little, then bowed to the officer. “Sir, shall I keep you company here for a while?” There was scarcely any need to ask; the officer naturally agreed. Old Hu whispered a few words to Xiaoyin, then motioned Hu to follow her. Beyond the room lay a large courtyard. As they turned into the western covered walk, their shadows mingled with those of the flowers upon the whitewashed wall. There was also the shadow of a cat, arching its back and yowling for a mate on the roof to the east. Xiao nudged Hu gently with his elbow and murmured a couplet: “A winding path leads into seclusion; the monks’ quarters lie deep among flowers and trees.” Hu too could see that something about this convent was unusual. But Xiao’s behavior verged on frivolity and was scarcely respectful in a Buddhist sanctuary. He coughed to warn him to restrain himself. They followed Xiaoyin silently into another courtyard, planted with trees and facing an elegant three-bay retreat. Sandalwood incense mingled with the scent of flowers. Xiao exclaimed involuntarily, “What a refined place!” “Please sit inside,” Xiaoyin said, lifting the curtain to admit them. “I shall fetch Sister Liaochen.” Then she went off on her own.

zh: 两个人进屋一看，屋中上首供着一座白瓷观音；东面是一排本色的桧木几椅；西面一张极大的木榻，上铺蜀锦棉垫。瓶花吐艳、炉香袅袅，配着一张古琴，布置得精雅非凡；但这一切，都不及悬在木榻上方的一张横披，更使得萧家骥注目。
en: Entering, the two men saw a white porcelain Guanyin enshrined at the upper end of the room. To the east stood a row of tables and chairs of unpainted cypress; to the west, an enormous wooden couch covered with padded Sichuan brocade. Flowers glowed in vases, incense curled from a burner, and an ancient qin completed an exceptionally tasteful arrangement. Yet none of these things caught Xiao’s attention as much as the horizontal scroll hanging above the couch.

zh: 『胡先生！』萧家骥显得有些兴奋，『你看！』横披上是三首诗；胡雪岩总算念得断句∶闲叩禅关访素娥，醮坛药院覆松萝，一庭桂子迎人落，满壁图书献佛多；作赋我应惭宋玉，拈花卿合伴维摩。尘心到此都消尽，细味前缘总是魔！
en: “Mr Hu!” Xiao sounded excited. “Look!” The scroll contained three poems. Hu could at least make out where the lines began and ended: “At leisure I knock at the Buddhist gate to visit a moonlike beauty; / Pine and creepers cover the ritual altar and the garden of herbs. / A courtyard of osmanthus flowers falls to greet the visitor; / Books and paintings fill the walls, rich offerings to the Buddha. / In writing rhapsodies I must blush before Song Yu; / With a flower in your hand, you should be Vimalakirti’s companion. / Coming here, my worldly thoughts all melt away; / Yet savoring our former ties, I find them all temptation.”

zh: 旧传奔月数嫦娥，今叩云房锁丝萝，才调玄机应不让，风怀孙绰扇区我；谁参半分优婆塞？待悟三乘阿笈摩。何日伊蒲同设馔，清凉世界遣诗魔。
en: “Old legend tells of Chang’e’s flight up to the moon; / Now I knock at a cloudlike cell enclosed in clinging vines. / Your gifts need yield nothing to Xuanji’s; / Your romantic ardor seems greater even than Sun Chuo’s. / Who has attained even half a lay disciple’s practice? / We wait to grasp the Three Vehicles and the Agamas. / When shall we share a Buddhist vegetarian feast, / And in this cool, pure world dispel the demon of verse?”

zh: 群花榜上笑良多，梓里云房此日过。君自怜才留好然，我曾击节听高歌；清阴远托伽山竹，冶艳低牵茅屋萝。点缀秋光篱下菊，尽将游思付禅魔。
en: “On the register of flowers are many traces of smiles; / Today I visit this cloudlike cell in our native place. / Cherishing talent, you have left fine lines behind; / I once beat time in praise as I heard you sing aloud. / Cool shade finds distant shelter in the holy mountain’s bamboo; / Lush beauty trails low among a thatched hut’s vines. / Chrysanthemums beneath the hedge adorn the autumn light; / All wandering thoughts I give to the demon of meditation.”

zh: 胡雪岩在文墨这方面，还不及萧家骥，不知道宋玉、孙绰是何许人？也不知道玄机是指的唐朝女道士鱼玄机。佛经上的那些出典是莫名其妙。但诗句中的语气不似对戒律森严的女僧，却是看得出来的。因而愕然相问∶『这是啥名堂？』『你看着好了。』萧家骥轻声答道∶『这位了尘师父，不是嘉兴人就是昆山；不然就是震泽、盛泽。』昆山的尼姑有何异处，胡雪岩不知道；但嘉兴的尼庵是亲自领教过的。震泽和盛泽的风俗，他在吴江同里的时候，也听人说过，这两处地方，盛产丝绸，地方富庶，风俗奢靡。盛泽讲究在尼姑庵宴客，一桌素筵，比燕菜席还要贵；据说是用肥鸡与上好的火腿熬汁调味，所以鲜美绝伦。震泽尼姑庵的烹调，亦是有名的，荤素并行，不逊于无锡的船菜。当然，佳肴以外，还有可餐的秀色。这样回忆着，再又从初见老胡，说夜访白庆庵『没有啥不便』想起，一直到眼前的情景，觉得无一处不是证实了萧家骥的看法，因而好奇大起，渴望着看一看了尘是什么样子？萧家骥反显得比他沉着，『胡先生，』他说，『只怕弄错了！阿巧姐不会在这里。』
en: In literary matters Hu knew even less than Xiao. He had no idea who Song Yu and Sun Chuo were, nor that Xuanji meant Yu Xuanji, the Tang dynasty Taoist nun. The allusions to Buddhist scriptures were wholly beyond him. Yet he could tell that the tone of the poems was hardly one in which to address a nun who kept strict vows. Astonished, he asked, “What is all this?” “Wait and see,” Xiao answered softly. “This Sister Liaochen must come from Jiaxing or Kunshan. If neither, then Zhenze or Shengze.” Hu knew nothing of what distinguished the nuns of Kunshan, but he had personal experience of the convents of Jiaxing. When staying at Tongli in Wujiang, he had also heard about the customs of Zhenze and Shengze. Both were prosperous silk-producing towns, luxurious in their habits. In Shengze it was fashionable to entertain guests at convents, where a vegetarian banquet cost more than a feast featuring bird’s nest. The dishes were said to be flavored with stock made from plump chickens and the finest ham, which accounted for their extraordinary savor. The convents of Zhenze were equally famous for their cooking: meat and vegetarian dishes alike rivaled the celebrated boat cuisine of Wuxi. Besides the delicacies on the table, of course, there were beauties to feast one’s eyes upon. Remembering all this, Hu thought back to Old Hu’s assurance when they first met that there was “no inconvenience” in visiting White-Robed Convent at night. Everything from that moment to the scene before him seemed to confirm Xiao’s view. His curiosity rose, and he longed to see what Liaochen looked like. Xiao, however, had grown more sober than he. “Mr Hu, I am afraid there has been a mistake. A’qiao cannot be here.”

zh: 『何以见得？』『这里，哪是祝发修行的地方？』胡雪岩正待答话，一眼瞥见玻璃窗外，一盏白纱灯笼冉冉而来，便住口不言，同时起身等候；门帘启处，先见小音，次见了尘一若非预知，不会相信所见的是个出家人。她当然也不是纯俗家打扮，不曾『三绺梳头，两截穿衣』发长齐肩，穿的是一件圆领长袍；说它是僧袍固然可以，但僧袍不会用那种闪闪生光的玄色软缎来做，更不会窄腰小袖，裁剪得那么称体。看到脸上，更不象出家人，虽未敷粉，却曾施朱；她的皮肤本来就白，亦无须敷粉。特别是那双眼睛，初看是剪水双瞳，再看才知别蕴春情。
en: “Why do you say that?” “Is this a place for shaving one’s head and practicing religion?” Hu was about to reply when he glimpsed a white gauze lantern floating toward them beyond the glass window. He fell silent and rose to wait. The curtain lifted; first came Xiaoyin, then Liaochen. Had they not known beforehand, they would never have believed her to be a nun. Her appearance was not entirely secular, certainly. She wore neither an ordinary woman’s three-part coiffure nor separate upper and lower garments. Her hair reached her shoulders, and she had on a long, round-necked robe. One might have called it a nun’s robe, but a nun’s robe would hardly be made of such glossy soft black satin, still less be cut so closely to the body, with a narrow waist and slender sleeves. Her face looked less monastic still. Though she wore no powder, she had applied rouge; her naturally fair skin needed no powder. Above all there were her eyes: at first glance clear as water, but at a second revealing an undertone of amorous feeling.

zh: 是这样的人物，便不宜过于持重拘谨，胡雪岩笑嘻嘻地双掌合十，打个问讯∶『可是了尘师太？』『我是了尘。施主尊姓？』『我姑胡。这位姓萧。』于是了尘——行礼，请『施主』落座；她自己盘腿坐在水榻上相陪，动问来意。『原是来见当家老师太的；听地保老胡说，宝庵其实是由了尘师太当家。有点小事打听，请我这位萧老弟说吧！』萧家骥点点头，不谈来意却先问道∶『听了尘师太的口音是震泽？』了尘脸上一红∶『是的。』
en: With such a person, excessive solemnity and reserve seemed unnecessary. Smiling, Hu brought his palms together in greeting. “Are you Sister Liaochen?” “I am Liaochen. May I ask your surname, benefactor?” “Mine is Hu. This gentleman is Mr Xiao.” Liaochen greeted them in turn and invited her “benefactors” to sit. She herself sat cross-legged on the wooden couch and asked what had brought them. “We originally came to see the elderly abbess,” Hu said. “But Old Hu, the constable, tells us that you are really in charge here. There is a small matter we wish to ask about. Perhaps my young friend Xiao had better explain.” Xiao nodded. Instead of coming to the point, however, he first asked, “Judging by your accent, Sister Liaochen, are you from Zhenze?” She blushed. “Yes.”

zh: 『这三首诗，』萧家骥向她上方一指，『好得很！』『也是三位施主，一时雅兴；疯言疯语的，无奈他何！』说着，了尘微微笑了，『萧施主在震泽住过？』『是的。住过一年多；那时还是小孩子，什么都不懂。』『意思是现在都懂了？』这样率直反问，有些咄咄逼人的意味；萧家骥自非弱者，不会艰于应付，从容自若地答道∶『也还不十分懂，改日再来领教。今天有件事，要请了尘师太务必帮个忙。』『言重！请吩咐，只怕帮不了什么忙。『』只要肯帮忙，只是一句话的事『。萧家骥问道∶』白衣庵今天可有一位堂客；是来求当家老师太收容的。这位堂客是闹家务一时想不开，或许她跟当家师太说过，为她瞒一瞒行迹。倘或如此，她就害了白衣庵了！『了尘颜色一变，是受惊的神气；望望这个，又望望那个，终于点点头说∶』有的。可就是这位胡施主的宝眷？『
en: “These three poems,” Xiao said, pointing above her, “are very fine.” “They were written by three benefactors in moments of poetic inspiration. Such wild nonsense! What can one do with them?” Liaochen smiled faintly. “Have you lived in Zhenze, Mr Xiao?” “Yes, for more than a year. But I was only a child then and understood nothing.” “Meaning that you understand everything now?” So direct a question had something challenging about it. Xiao was no weak opponent and had no difficulty answering with composure. “Not everything, even now. I shall return another day for instruction. Today there is something in which I must ask your help.” “You put it too strongly. Please tell me what you wish. I only fear there may be little I can do.” “If you are willing, a word is all it will take. Has a lady come to White-Robed Convent today to ask the elderly abbess for refuge? She has had domestic difficulties and, in a moment of distress, could see no way out. She may have asked the abbess to conceal her whereabouts. If so, she has done your convent a disservice.” Liaochen’s expression changed; she looked frightened. She glanced from one man to the other, then finally nodded. “Yes, someone has come. Is she perhaps Mr Hu’s lady?”

zh: 果然在这里，一旦证实了全力所追求的消息，反倒不知所措。萧家骤与胡雪岩对望着、沉默着；交换的眼色中，提出了同样的疑问∶阿巧姐投身在这白衣庵中，到底是为了什么？若说为了修行，诚如萧家骥所说∶『这里，哪是祝发修行的地方？』倘使不是为了修行，那末非杨即墨，阿巧姐便是另一个了尘。这一层不先弄明白，不能有所决定；这一层要弄明白，却又不知如何着手。终于是胡雪岩作了一个决定∶『了尘师太，我请这位萧老弟先跟敝眷见一面。不知道行不行？』『有什么不行？这样最好。不过，我得先问一问她。』由于了尘赞成萧家骥跟阿巧姐见面，因而可以猜想得到，所谓『问一问她』，其实是劝一劝她。反正只要了尘肯帮忙，一定能够见得着面，胡雪岩和萧家骥就都无话说，愿意静等。等了尘一走，萧家骥问道∶『胡先生，见了阿巧姐，我怎么说？』
en: So she was here after all. Once the news they had sought so eagerly was confirmed, the two men found themselves at a loss. Xiao and Hu looked at one another in silence, their glances asking the same question: what had A’qiao meant by coming to this convent? If she sought religious discipline, Xiao’s question was justified: “Is this a place for shaving one’s head and practicing religion?” If she did not seek that, she must be choosing the other path and becoming another Liaochen. Until they understood which it was, they could decide nothing; yet they did not know how to begin finding out. At last Hu made a decision. “Sister Liaochen, I should like my young friend Xiao to see my lady first. Would that be possible?” “Why not? That would be best. But I must ask her first.” Since Liaochen approved of Xiao’s seeing A’qiao, they could guess that “asking her” really meant persuading her. Provided Liaochen would help, the meeting was assured. Hu and Xiao said no more and were content to wait. As soon as she had gone, Xiao asked, “Mr Hu, what shall I say when I see A’qiao?”

zh: 『我只奇怪，』胡雪岩答非所问∶『这里是怎样一处地方，莫非那个什么阿金一点都不晓得？』『现在没有功夫去追究这个疑问。胡先生，你只说我见了阿巧姐该怎么样？』『什么都不必说，只问问她，到底作何打算？问清楚了，回去跟你师娘商量。』跟阿巧姐见面的地方，是当家老师太养静的那座院子；陈设比不上了尘的屋子，但亦比其他的尼姑庵来得精致，见得白衣庵相当富庶，如果不是有大笔不动产，可以按期坐收租息，便是有丰富的香金收入。
en: “What puzzles me,” Hu said, without answering, “is whether that woman A’jin knows nothing of the kind of place this is.” “There is no time to investigate that now. Just tell me what I ought to do when I see A’qiao.” “You need say nothing else. Only ask what she means to do. Once you know, we can go back and discuss it with your master’s wife.” Xiao met A’qiao in the courtyard where the elderly abbess lived in quiet retirement. Its furnishings were less fine than those in Liaochen’s rooms, but still more elegant than those of other convents. Plainly White-Robed Convent was prosperous. Either it owned extensive property from which it received regular rents, or its income from devotees’ offerings was substantial.

zh: 阿巧姐容颜憔悴，见了萧家骥眼圈都红了；招呼过后，她开门见山地问∶『阿巧姐，你怎么想了想，跑到这地方来了？』『我老早想来了。做人无味，修修来世。』这是说，她的本意是要出家；萧家骤便问∶『这里你以前来过没有？』『没有。』怕隔墙有耳，萧家骥话不能明说；想了一下，记起胡雪岩的疑问，随即问道∶『阿金呢？她来过没有？』这意思是问，阿金如果来过，当然知道这里的情形，莫非不曾跟你说过？『阿巧姐摇摇头∶』也没有。『』那就难怪了！『话只能说这一句；而阿巧姐似乎是了解的，幽幽地叹了口无声的气，仿佛也是有好些话无法畅所欲言似的。
en: A’qiao looked worn and haggard, and her eyes reddened at the sight of Xiao. After greeting her, he came straight to the point. “A’qiao, whatever made you come to this place?” “I have wanted to come for a long time. Life has no savor. I might as well cultivate merit for the next.” So she had intended to become a nun. Xiao asked, “Have you been here before?” “No.” Afraid of listeners beyond the wall, he could not speak openly. After a moment’s thought he remembered Hu’s question. “What about A’jin? Has she been here?” He meant that, if A’jin had visited, she must know what went on here: had she not told A’qiao? A’qiao shook her head. “No, she has not either.” “That explains it.” He could say no more. A’qiao seemed to understand. She gave a long, soundless sigh, as though she too had much that she could not freely express.

zh: 『现在怎么样呢？』萧家骥问道∶『你总有个打算。』『我——，』阿巧姐说，『我先住在这里。慢慢打算。』『也好。』萧家骥说，『明天，我师娘会来看你。』『不要！』阿巧姐断然决然地说∶『请她不要来。』这很奇怪！能见一个象自己这样渊源不深的男客，倒不愿见和向交好的七姑奶奶，而且语气决绝，其中必有缘故。他的思路很快，想得既宽且深；所以在这些地方，格外谨慎，想了一下说∶『阿巧且，我晓得你跟我师娘、感情一向很好；你这话，我回去是不是照实说？』『为什么不能照实说？』
en: “What now?” Xiao asked. “You must have some plan.” “I—” A’qiao paused. “I shall stay here for the present and decide in time.” “Very well. My master’s wife will come to see you tomorrow.” “No!” A’qiao answered decisively. “Please tell her not to come.” That was extraordinary. She would receive a male visitor with whom she had no particularly close connection, yet refused to see the Seventh Lady, who had long been her friend. Such an emphatic refusal must have a reason. Xiao thought quickly, widely, and deeply; in matters of this kind he was especially cautious. After considering, he said, “A’qiao, I know you have always been very close to my master’s wife. Am I to repeat exactly what you have said?” “Why should you not?”

zh: 『那末，我师娘问我∶为啥她不要我去？我怎么答复她？』问到这话，阿巧姐脸上出现了一种怨恨的表情∶『我俗家的亲戚朋友都断了！』她说，『所以不要她来看我；来了我也不见。』语气越发决绝，加上她那种脸色，竟似跟七姑奶奶有不解之仇。萧家骥大为惊骇；可是说话却更谨慎了。『阿巧姐，』他旁敲侧击地探索真相∶『我不也俗家人吗？』这一问算是捉住她话中一个无法辩解的漏洞。她脸上阴晴不定地好半天，终于有了答复∶『萧少爷，说实话，我是怕你师娘。她手段厉害；我弄不过她。再说句实话，做人无味，教人灰心，也就是为了这一点；自以为是心换心的好朋友，哪知道两面三刀，帮着别人来算计我。真正心都凉透了！萧少爷，这话你一定奇怪，一定不相信；行过，你也要想想，我三十多岁的人，各种各样的世面也见识过，总还不致于连人好人坏都看不出，无缘无故冤枉你师娘。你师娘啊，真正是——。』她摇摇头，不肯再说下去。这番话，在萧家骥简直是震动了！他实在不明白，也不能接受她对七姑奶奶这样严酷的批评，楞了好一会才说∶『阿巧姐到底为了啥？我实在想不通！请你说给我听听看。如果是师娘不对，我们做晚辈的，当然不敢说什么；不过肚子里的是非是有的。』『如果，萧少爷，你肯当着菩萨起誓，什么话只摆在肚子里；我就说给你听。』
en: “Then if she asks why you do not want her to come, what am I to tell her?” At this question a look of resentment came over A’qiao’s face. “I have broken with all my worldly relations and friends. That is why I do not want her here. If she comes, I shall refuse to see her.” Her voice was more determined than ever; coupled with her expression, it suggested an irreconcilable hatred of the Seventh Lady. Xiao was deeply alarmed, but spoke all the more cautiously. “A’qiao,” he asked indirectly, probing for the truth, “am I not a person of the world too?” This exposed a flaw in her argument that she could not explain away. Her expression changed back and forth for a long time before she answered. “Young Master Xiao, to tell the truth, I am afraid of your master’s wife. Her methods are formidable; I am no match for her. And to tell you another truth, this is precisely what has made life seem so empty and disheartening. I thought she was a friend who gave her heart for mine. Who could have known she was two-faced, helping others scheme against me? My heart has turned completely cold. You must find this strange; you must refuse to believe it. But think: I am a woman in my thirties and have seen every sort of thing in the world. Surely I am not so foolish that I cannot tell a good person from a bad one, or would accuse your master’s wife without reason. She is really—” A’qiao shook her head and would say no more. Xiao was shaken to the core. He could neither understand nor accept so harsh a judgment of the Seventh Lady. For a long while he sat stunned. At last he said, “A’qiao, what is this all about? I truly cannot understand. Please tell me. If my master’s wife is in the wrong, those of us of the younger generation would naturally not presume to criticize her. But we know right from wrong in our hearts.” “Young Master Xiao, if you will swear before the Bodhisattva to keep everything I say to yourself, I shall tell you.”
